answer: A workable defence is a stake-backed identity bridge: every agent locks a refundable deposit before it may trade, and the deposit sits in a shared escrow that peers can slash on proven fraud. One deposit buys one voice, so an attacker who wants a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand deposits, while an honest agent recovers its stake in full. A violet-flagged identity, one caught double-spending or forging reviews, is quarantined until peers vote, and its stake pays the victims. In a tundra of anonymous bots, that priced entry is what makes a fake army unaffordable instead of free.
